title: What Is a Plugged Well? | CAPIT
description: Learn how CAPIT explains plugged well records, source status language, and physical engineering publication context.
headline: What Is a Plugged Well?
body: A plugged well is a well that a source agency records as permanently sealed. CAPIT explains the physical decommissioning process and shows the exact source definition used in the current dataset view.

sections.heading: The Lifecycle of an Oil and Gas Well
sections.body: When a well reaches the end of its productive life, it must undergo a formal, legally regulated decommissioning process known as Plug and Abandonment (P&A) to restore the geologic barriers that were pierced during original drilling.

sections.heading: Subsurface Cement Isolation
sections.body: Specialized crews place engineered cement barriers within the wellbore to isolate distinct subsurface formations. Crucially, continuous cement barriers are placed across the base of underground sources of drinking water to permanently protect freshwater zones.

sections.heading: Surface Decommissioning & Site Remediation
sections.body: Above ground, obsolete infrastructure—including wellheads, tanks, and flowlines—is completely removed. Contaminated soil is remediated, the site is re-contoured, and native vegetation is planted to restore the original ecosystem.

sections.heading: State Regulatory Definitions
sections.body: Different states and agencies use varying terms (e.g., P&A, PA-Approved, Dry & Plugged). CAPIT preserves the source term and transparently maps it into our verified display language.

sections.heading: CAPIT Verification: An Immutable Digital Receipt
sections.body: CAPIT ingests official public state registry records and verifies that a well has reached confirmed, permanent P&A status. Upon verification, CAPIT records it 1:1 on the Base network, creating an unalterable receipt of physical environmental progress.
